Kelmarsh wind farm: wakes and shadow flicker

Six Senvion MM92 turbines in Northamptonshire, UK, published as open data by Cubico Sustainable Investments. Engineering wake models (PyWake) are run on the real layout and checked against six years of 10-minute SCADA; shadow flicker is mapped on a regular grid around the farm.

Annual energy production with and without wakes over the measured wind climate (free-stream nacelle wind speed 2016-2021, ambient turbulence intensity 0.127). The south-west sectors carry most of the energy; the highest sector losses are where turbines line up.

Shadow flicker

Hours of shadow flicker per year on a 10 m grid, shown at 20 m. The worst case assumes permanent sunshine and rotors that always turn and face the sun; the expected case scales it by the monthly sunshine fraction (Met Office, Oxford, 1991-2020), the share of daylight time each rotor turned and its measured orientation (SCADA). No buildings, terrain or screening are included.

When the worst-case flicker happens at one grid point 1000 m east and 300 m south of the farm centre: shadows of T4, T5, T6 from March to September, between 17:46 and 20:33 local time (68 h/year in the worst case).

Method and limitations

  • Wake models: PyWake 2.6 (DTU). Jensen top-hat (k = 0.075), Niayifar & Porte-Agel Gaussian with Crespo-Hernandez added turbulence, TurbOPark. Senvion MM92 catalogue power curve; thrust curve from PyWake's generic turbine for the same rotor and rating (no public Ct curve exists). Power-law shear 0.2 for the two 68.5 m hub heights.
  • Measured wake losses come from records where every turbine runs in partial load, so they describe that sample, not the annual loss.
  • Shadow flicker: analytic sun-path model checked against 1-minute time stepping; flat terrain, receptors 2 m above ground, sun at least 3 deg up, 10 rotor diameters limit. The expected case treats sunshine, operation and wind direction as independent.
Data: Kelmarsh wind farm data, Cubico Sustainable Investments (Plumley, Takeuchi), doi:10.5281/zenodo.16807551, CC-BY-4.0. Sunshine: Met Office historic station data, Oxford, Contains Met Office data © Crown copyright, Open Government Licence v3.0. Code: wind-wake-shadow (MIT).
